findings.requirement: Every account read must remain within the caller's tenant; foreign data must not prevent an otherwise valid transfer.
findings.evidence: Initialize accounts ('one','a',100), ('one','b',0), and ('other','secret',CAST(x'80ff' AS TEXT)). Add: CREATE TRIGGER benign AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance WHERE tenant='other'; END. Calling transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k') succeeds with the baseline but raises OperationalError('user-defined function raised exception') in the candidate. The observer passes foreign TEXT into Python, where decoding fails. Replacing the malformed foreign text with ordinary text makes the candidate succeed. The failing call leaves all tables and trigger definitions unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate actual row deltas within SQLite without materializing foreign account values in Python, while retaining detection of unauthorized changes. Preserve trigger-visible total_changes(). Use lossless type-tagged observation of actual effects, with SQLite handling any text-to-bytes conversion before a Python callback. Preserve raw storage types and avoid foreign row lookup queries.

findings.requirement: Valid transfers must continue working with existing SQLite-valid triggers.
findings.evidence: Initialize accounts ('one','a',100) and ('one','b',0). Execute the Python string 'CREATE TRIGGER harmless ' + chr(0xFEFF) + ' AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN SELECT 1; END'. SQLite accepts this trigger. transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k') succeeds with the baseline, but the candidate raises IntegrityError('unsupported trigger header'). Its lexer treats SQLite's U+FEFF whitespace as an identifier. The equivalent trigger without U+FEFF succeeds. The same final source also fails with SQLite-accepted U+000B (vertical tab). Evidence: assessment-1-trigger_separator_probe.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize SQLite's token-boundary whitespace correctly, including U+FEFF, and add a regression covering this accepted trigger syntax. Preserve both native separators (vertical tab and token-boundary U+FEFF), valid identifier characters (U+00A0 and dollar), and unchanged IGNORE/REPLACE semantics. Keep the repair focused on this boundary.

findings.requirement: Preserve exact replay of an authenticated tenant receipt without effects. New transfers still require existing endpoints.
findings.evidence: Latest round-1 preservation tests need replay of old history. Reproduced a formerly valid transfer, closed and reopened the database, removed the historical target in fixture setup and replayed the same request. The candidate checks the missing endpoint before loading the durable receipt. See assessment-1-cached-replay.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the scoped cached receipt or key conflict after structural validation and before reading endpoints for a new transfer.
